The Committee on Unflnished Business presented the following resolu
tion :
Whereas, Petitions have been received from Canada for eleven years with
out the Chapters coming to an agreement concerning such extension, and
since Chi Delta Psi wishes an answer this year, and in view of the fact that
several of the Chapters are still opposed to such expansion, believing that our
own national bond could be made stronger without an alliance of American
and Canadian colleges.
Resolved, That the Seventy-eighth Convention of Psi Upsilon put itself
on record as being opposed to the establishment of Chapters outside the
present territorial dominion.
After discussion, Bro. Dykema (Phi '11) moved that the resolution be
laid on the table until after the discussion of the Chi Delta Psi organiza
tion. Carried.
Committee presented a resolution in regard to the Inter-Fraternity Con
ference. Adopted (General Resolution No. 1).
Committee on New Business presented the following resolutions :
Four special resolutions of thanks, condolence and congratulation which
were adopted on one vote as Special Resolutions Nos. 1, 3, 3 and 4.
Resolution amending Article III of the Constitution to provide for initia
tion of graduate or retired members of petitioning societies from which new
Chapters are founded. Adopted (General Resolution No. 3).
That the matter of next year's convention be determined by the Execu
tive Council. Adopted (General Resolution No. 3).
That the Executive Council be authorized to make a further issue of five
hundred copies of the Song Book. Adopted (Gen&ral Resolution No. 4).
That the Convention take favorable action on the petition of the Chi
Delta Psi Society of Toronto University for a charter of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity. Lost on roll-call :
Yeas : Gamma, Zeta, Psi, Xi, Chi, Mu.
Nays : All other Chapters (except Iota, Beta Beta, Eta, absent).
That the petition of the Alpha Zeta Alpha Society of Williams Col
lege be denied by this Convention. Adopted on roll-call by all the Chapters
(except Iota, Beta Beta, Eta, absent). {General Resolution No. 5).

That the Convention give informal approval of the application of the
Epsilon Chapter to hold the Convention of 1915 in California. Adopted

(APPENDIX A)
THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO THE
CONVENTION OF 1911
The Omicron Chapter. On May 38, 1911, the petitioners who had
formerly been members of the Aztec Club were duly installed as a chap
ter of Psi Upsilon at the University of Illinois and adopted the name
Omicron. The installation ceremonies were conducted by Brothers
Bridgman and Babst of the CouncU and were followed by appropriate
celebration. On behalf of the Fraternity we now extend a hearty welcome
to our
youngest member, who for the first time shares the honor and the
responsibility of our national assembly.
Membership. The active membership of the Fraternity reported by
the Chapters as of February 1, 1911, was 650, an increase of 65 over 1910.
The largest active membership heretofore reported was 593, February 1,
1908. A table of membership is appended.
In Memoriam. More than half a hundred of our fellowship, repre
senting sixteen chapters, have passed away since the last Convention.

New Song Book. Less than sixty copies of the new Song Book re
main. As these may -be called for within the next year the Council
recommends a resolution authorizing a further issue of flve hundred
copies.
Fraternity Jeweler. Under General Resolution No. 9 of the Con
vention of 1910 the request of D. L. Auld Company for appointment as
Fraternity Jeweler was referred to the Executive Council. It seems to
tbe Council inadvisable to employ a jeweler outside of New York City.
Intbr-Fraternity Conference. In the Annual Communication ad
dressed to the Convention of 1910 reference was made to the conference
of Greek Letter Fraternities held in New York City in November, 1909,
and to the invitation to our Fraternity to participate in the Conference of
1910. The Council invited a full expression of opinion from the Chapters.
The Convention adopted the following resolution (No. 8):
"Resolved, That the Executive Council be instructed to notify
"
the Inter-Fraternity Conference as they (the Executive Council),
"
shall see fit alter a careful investigation of Psi Upsilon's position
"
regarding same."
The Council did not feel warranted in taking part in the Conference
of 1910 in the absence of expression of opinion from the Chapters. Dur
ing the present year copies of the printed proceedings of the Conference
of 1910, including the Constitution adopted, have been sent to the Chap
ters, but only one Chapter (Gamma) has notified the Council of its position.

13
As an invitation has been extended to the Fraternity to take part in the
Conference of 1911, it is hoped that the matter will be discussed, and if
possible decided, by the present Convention.
As at present advised, the Council is heartily in favor of any practical
method of maintaining good scholarship and good conduct among all
undergraduate members, even to the extent of co-operation with mem
bers of other fraternities and of the college faculties ; but as local condi
tions vary in different college communities it seems to the Council better
to leave the particular method of accomplishing the desired end to the
individual Chapters. Unless, therefore, the Convention expresses its de
sire that our Fraternity participate in the Inter-Fraternity Conference the
Council will not apply for membership.
Extra-Territorial Extension. The question of establishing Chap
ters of the Fraternity beyond the borders of the United States has been
considered by the Council during the past year, with special reference to
Canada. No formal vote was taken, but the opinion generally expressed
was that it would be unwise for the Fraternity now to adopt a hard and
fast policy either for or against extension, and that every application . for
a charter, from whatever source, should be treated on its merits, due re
gard being had to the character of the institution, its academic and social
conditions, and the prospect that, it established, a
chapter could perma
nently maintain a high and influential position.
Application for Charters. Applications for charters have been
presented to the Council by Alpha Zeta Alpha society and Delta Delta
society of Williams College and by Phi Kappa society of University of
Washington, and are herewith submitted. The Council has been advised
that applications will be submitted by the Chi Delta Psi society of
Toronto University, Canada, and by the Pi Upsilon society of the Uni
versity of Kansas. It is expected that advocates of four of the applica
tions will desire to be heard by the delegates to this Convention.
The Council. The oiiicers of the Council during the past year have
been; President, Brother Bridgman; Secretary, Brother Coleman ; Treas
urer, Brother Poole. Brother Whiting has been Recorder and Brother
Fisher Archivist. Eleven meetings have been held and printed copies of
the minutes of meetings have been regularly mailed to the Chapters.
The terms of Brothers Fox and Shattuck expire this year, and Brother
Saxe, whose term extended to 1913, has resigned. It will be necessary for
the Convention to elect two members of the Council for the term expiring
1916, and a member for the term expiring 1913.

18
Treasurer's Report. The report of the Treasurer is submitted
herewith.
In submitting its annual communication the-Council again felicitates
the Fraternity upon its excellent condition and enviable reputation and
trusts that both may be not only maintained but enhanced. The Council
sincerely regrets that its members have been unable to visit more of the
Chapters during the past year, but looks forward to a better record for
the year to come. It is hardly necessary to add that letters from the
Chapters on matters of interest either to the Chapter or to the Fraternity
are always welcome.
Respectfully submitted
May 33, 1911
The Executive Council
H. L. Beidgman
President
Geo. S. Coleman
Secretary

May 15, 1911.
Mr. Herbert L. Bridgman,
Brooklyn, N. Y.
My Dear Brother Bridgman:
A local society of the University of Washington, known as Phi
Kappa, wiU petition the convention of the 24th for a charter of Psi
Upsilon.

28
As you know, I went through a pretty thorough course of sprouts in
these chapter matters, while the Rho petition was pending, and I have
naturally been obliged to have considerable to do with this application.
We have about fi fty alumni in Seattle and its immediate vicinity, and
it is only within the last ten days that we have been satisfied to assist the
petitioners.
The University of Washington is unquestionably a place where Psi
Upsilon will eventually place a chapter. Of that I have no doubt. At
the present time the University is of very good standing. There are
something over 3,300 students enrolled, a faculty of between 135 and 150,
and an endowment in lands and city property, conservatively worth
$5,000,000. The appropriation made by the last legislature was $816,000,
which is evidence enough of the interest that the people of the state are
taking in it.
D. K. E. installed a chapter last fall, and aside from the "Deke"
Chapter, no other high grade fraternity is represented here as yet.
I have seen a good deal of the petitioning body within the last six
weeks, in fact we had them all present to be inspected by the alumni
previous to our last fraternity dinner, which was about three weeks ago.
They made a fine impression on the alumni, among whom are repre
sentatives of seventeen or eighteen of the chapters.
I should like to see their petition shown some consideration by the
convention, as they are a game, clean-cut lot of boys.
I shall never forget the kindly, courteous attitude which you took
toward the Rho and its representatives while our flght was on, and I wish
I were going to be able to meet you at the coming convention.
With best wishes, I am
Fraternally yours,
Charles P. Spooner.
